intervention_label: Gating workup run concurrently with induction: high-resolution HLA class I typing (A*02:01 / A*24:02) plus HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of the patient AND the sibling donor, quantitative CD33/CD123 antigen density, TP53 variant-level CNV-capable NGS, and organ-function documentation (CrCl, LFTs, ejection fraction)
expected_benefit: Resolves the allele-level HLA-A*02:01 (and A*24:02) status and the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative direction that gate the two HLA-restricted rows below; clears the CD33 >=20% screening gate on NCT04050280; determines whether the TP53 lesion is Y220C; and supplies the organ-function numbers every toxicity claim on this board is currently missing.
key_risks: None from the assays themselves (blood draw, marrow aspirate, archival material, records request)
Delay is the only harm, and it is real: peripheral blasts moved 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, so this runs alongside cycle 1 of the rank-2 cytoreduction rather than in front of it
HA-1/HA-2 genotyping at rs1801284 is not a routine US send-out (1-3 weeks) and needs a fresh sibling sample plus donor consent
preference_alignment: matches the stated priority (surface and de-risk the HLA-restricted pathway): YES; matches the free-text request that the 0.75 efficacy weight be revisited once fitness is known: YES; no toxicity veto or modality constraint touches it.
guideline_status: Not a therapy. NCCN AML v3.2026 evaluation already includes high-resolution HLA typing where allogeneic HCT is contemplated, plus liver and renal chemistries and cardiac assessment after cardiotoxic exposure; HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is the one item no guideline orders.
rationale_summary: Conservative ranked this first and concensusite endorsed it on guideline grounds, since NCCN's own AML evaluation already orders high-resolution HLA typing when transplant is contemplated. Risktaker dissented and critic and advocate filed qualified agreements, and all three objections were the same one: a workup is not a therapy, and rank 1 on a lab requisition reads to the patient as wait while peripheral blasts moved 58% to 82% in a fortnight. The row stays at rank 1 because a pending biomarker decides whether the conditional rows below exist at all, and the objection is answered by making it concurrent rather than sequential: these assays run alongside cycle 1 of the rank-2 cytoreduction. One item inside it is not like the others. HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of the patient and the sibling carries a manufacturing lead time nothing else here has, because a fresh donor collection cannot begin until the sibling genotype returns, so it goes out the same day as the ejection fraction rather than after a response is documented. The agreement score of 0.2 is the board's signal about ordering, not about the assays, which every persona wants run.
open_questions: Whether the ~2020 allele-level typing report can be retrieved and confirmed without a re-draw
Whether the HA-1 mismatch runs in the required direction (recipient rs1801284 A/G or A/A, donor G/G)
Whether HLA loss or class I downregulation on sorted blasts has already silenced the A*02:01 restriction (6p LOH by NGS/SNP array plus surface class I flow)
Whether the 2019 TP53 lesion was Y220C, and whether 17p FISH or p53 IHC explains the 2026 negative on a 2%-LOD, no-CNV panel
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic gate, not a therapy: opens or closes the entire HLA-restricted axis, clears the CD33 screening gate, and prices every toxicity claim on the board.
toxicity_burden: Low (none - diagnostic testing on blood, marrow and archival material)
overall: The master switch and the lead-time item in one requisition: run it during induction, not before, because the sibling HA-1 genotype gates a fresh donor collection.

intervention_label: CLAG-GO: cladribine, high-dose cytarabine and G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 (NCT04050280)
expected_benefit: Cytoreduction that makes everything downstream reachable. Fractionated gemtuzumab monotherapy produced 26% CR in first relapse (n=57) with no grade 3-4 hepatic toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease, seven of those patients transplanted afterwards; the CLAG backbone supplies the depth. CLAG-GO itself has no published efficacy in refractory AML.
key_risks: Prolonged grade 4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia in a six-year-old graft; median neutropenia 23 days in the fractionated-gemtuzumab series
Calicheamicin hepatotoxicity including veno-occlusive disease: fractionation lowers the risk, it does not zero it, and another conditioning regimen is planned within months
Nucleoside cross-resistance after progression on FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax
No creatinine clearance, LFTs or ejection fraction on file to price any of this against
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials (NCT04050280 recruiting, and the regimen can be rebuilt from marketed drugs at the home centre if the slot does not open): YES; matches the efficacy-leaning 0.75 weight: YES, but that weight was set before fitness was documented and the free text asks for it to be revisited; no toxicity veto applies (the list is empty).
guideline_status: NCCN AML v3.2026 puts clinical trial first for relapsed/refractory disease and lists both halves separately: cladribine/cytarabine/G-CSF in the intensive R/R chemotherapy table, and gemtuzumab ozogamicin as the CD33-positive option, on-label for R/R CD33+ AML. Gemtuzumab is absent from the poor-risk induction options while present for favourable and intermediate risk.
rationale_summary: All five personas ranked CLAG-GO, four of them first or second, and the reason is arithmetic rather than enthusiasm: at roughly 85% marrow blasts nearly everything else here is gated on cytoreduction, with CBX-250 wanting WBC under 25,000, the interferon-gamma DLI protocol capping blasts at 30%, MT-401-OTS at 10%, and the favourable second-transplant strata requiring blasts under 27-35%. NCT04050280 is the one strong-fit open trial in the file, with refractoriness after an intensive regimen required, AML arising from prior haematologic disease eligible, and relapse after allogeneic transplant explicitly permitted at 60 days or more provided GVHD is at most grade 1. What the board would not let stand is the expectation. ALFA-0701 enrolled untreated de novo AML and specifically excluded secondary and therapy-related disease, which is her diagnosis, and the 3,325-patient individual-patient-data meta-analysis puts adverse cytogenetics at OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.83-1.18, p=0.9), the strongest evidence in this dossier and null for her karyotype. That changes what to expect from the gemtuzumab component rather than where the regimen ranks, because the CLAG backbone plus a documented pre-transplant hepatic safety record at 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 is what earns the slot. Entry turns on CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, which the qualitative flow result does not establish, so the quantitative density request sitting in the rank-1 workup is on this regimen's critical path too.
open_questions: Quantitative CD33 antigen density (ABC/MESF) - the NCT04050280 screening gate and the ALFA-0701 flow reanalysis both turn on expression level, not on a positive-or-negative call
Whether the right-thigh myeloid sarcoma answers to a marrow-directed CD33 regimen; paired series detect CD33 in about 79% of lesions
Baseline bilirubin, transaminases and an ejection fraction before dose one
Whether the Baltimore slot opens, or whether the regimen is rebuilt off-protocol at the home centre
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate as cytoreduction: CLAG backbone with a CD33 payload, but no published CLAG-GO efficacy in refractory AML and Hills 2014 null in her karyotype.
toxicity_burden: High (prolonged grade 4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia and infection, calicheamicin hepatotoxicity including veno-occlusive disease)

counter_productive_moa.description: Nucleoside cross-resistance after FLAG-IDA failure; prolonged aplasia in a six-year-old graft could end the transplant plan rather than enable it.

overall: The gate on almost everything else here: the one strong-fit open trial accepting post-allograft relapse, with a CD33 component the randomised data do not support in her karyotype.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) from the HLA-identical sibling on a cytoreduce-first or sequential-conditioning platform (e.g. DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC, NCT06928662)
expected_benefit: The only option in this dossier with a documented cure fraction. In her stratum, a related-donor first graft, 2-year OS was 37% +/- 6% versus 16% +/- 4% after an unrelated first graft; across 2,632 second transplants 5-year relapse-free survival was 15%. Blasts under 27% carry HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.40-0.72, p<0.001) for survival.
key_risks: Non-relapse mortality after a second graft, which none of the four registries tabulates - the harm side of every quoted survival curve is missing
Acute and chronic GVHD, prolonged cytopenias, infection
Conditioning intensity cannot be chosen without a cardiac and renal baseline that does not exist
The US sequential protocol asks her to repeat a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through
Marrow-directed conditioning does not treat the thigh sarcoma, which needs its own local plan
preference_alignment: matches the stated curative intent and the explicit acceptance of HCT2 as a modality: YES; matches prefers_trials via NCT06928662: PARTIAL (an institutional sequential regimen is the likelier route); efficacy-leaning 0.75 weight: YES, pending the fitness revisit her own free text asks for.
guideline_status: No NCCN category and no ELN grade attaches to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse; both pathways assume a first transplant. NCCN AML v3.2026 tells you to start the donor search at first relapse, and ELN 2022 recommends allogeneic HCT once cytoreduction is achieved. Read this as uncovered rather than contraindicated.
rationale_summary: All five personas put a second allograft in their top four and critic ranked it first; nothing else here has a documented cure fraction. Concensusite established the guideline gap and it should be read as uncovered rather than contraindicated, since NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022 both describe cytoreduction then transplant but neither attaches a category to a second graft after post-transplant relapse. Critic's reconciliation is the formulation to carry: a missing category is not missing evidence, but what backs HCT2 is four registries (n=2632, 399, 263, 179) replicating a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect, with selection into a second graft unadjusted in every one of them, because who gets offered a second transplant is itself a fitness judgement made by the treating centre. Her stratum is favourable on nearly every axis those registries measure: a related-donor first graft at 2-year OS 37% +/- 6%, a six-year first remission far past the five-month cut that drives the EBMT score, a sibling donor already collected once. The single exception decides the sequencing, because Schmid's score gives blasts under 27% an HR of 0.53 (0.40-0.72, p<0.001) and puts the worst band at 4% +/- 2% at two years, and at roughly 85% she sits in that worst band today. HCT2 is the destination and rank 2 is the gate; taking her to conditioning as the marrow stands spends the non-relapse mortality without buying the survival.
open_questions: Non-relapse mortality for a second graft in her specific fitness band - not tabulated in any registry row
Conditioning intensity, which cannot be chosen without a measured ejection fraction and creatinine clearance
Whether HLA loss or class II downregulation on the relapsed blasts explains the first escape, in which case the same sibling repertoire will not fix it
Whether a germline predisposition shared with the sibling redirects donor choice (needs cultured fibroblasts, not blood, while blasts circulate)
Local control of the right-thigh myeloid sarcoma
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate if cytoreduced, low as she stands: four registries replicate 2-year OS 37% +/- 6% in her donor stratum, all gated on blasts under 27-35%.
toxicity_burden: High (non-relapse mortality after a second graft, acute and chronic GVHD, prolonged cytopenias, infection; no registry row tabulates per-organ adverse events)

counter_productive_moa.description: The same sibling repertoire that already lost control; HLA loss or class II downregulation would defeat graft-versus-leukaemia a second time.

overall: The only documented cure fraction here, backed by four registries replicating a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect, and gated entirely on getting blasts under 27%.

scenario_label: If HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed at allele level with a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch
intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921), as post-cytoreduction or post-graft consolidation
expected_benefit: Krakow 2024: CR achieved or maintained in 4 of 9 infused post-allo-HCT relapses, one MRD-negative beyond 27 months, with no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS. The registered primary endpoint is manufacturing feasibility and DLT, so 44.4% is a descriptive secondary and not a response rate.
key_risks: Grade 3-5 infections after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow, and one grade 4 infusion reaction in 9
Two mild grade 1-2 acute GVHD cases, attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal before infusion rather than to the cells
No patient in the series was infused after a second allograft, so the HCT2 interaction is unmeasured rather than reassuring
Collection, manufacture and lymphodepletion take weeks against a marrow that moved 58% to 82% in a month
preference_alignment: matches the explicit reason for the run (HLA-restricted immunotherapy eligibility): YES; matches prefers_trials including travel with geography_band null: YES; toxicity_vetoes and modality_constraints are both empty, so nothing in her file blocks it.
guideline_status: No guideline lists HA-1 TCR-T - not NCCN AML v3.2026, not ELN 2022, not the EBMT DLI recommendations. What is guideline-endorsed is the route: NCCN names clinical trial as strongly preferred for R/R disease, and high-resolution HLA typing already sits in NCCN's own AML workup, so pulling the 2020 allele-level report is guideline-concordant care rather than a research errand.
rationale_summary: This is the reason the case was submitted, and advocate ranked it first. In round 2 advocate conceded the ordering, but conceded to one specific argument and not to the others: risktaker's tumour-burden case, that an A*02:01-restricted WT1 TCR gave median OS 242 days in post-transplant disease with only 2 of 15 carrying overt disease, and that Medigene read tumour burden as the limiting factor in their own PRAME phase 1. That concession is about therapy order, not action order. The HLA record pull and HA-1 genotyping of the patient and the sibling belong in the rank-1 workup running now, during induction, because a fresh donor collection cannot start until the sibling genotype returns and nothing else on the list carries that lead time; holding it until a response is documented restarts the manufacturing clock at the moment the window is best. Critic's dissent persists at any rank and is not biomarker-contingent: NCT03326921's registered primary endpoint is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity, so 4 of 9 is a descriptive secondary, and the denominator mixes patients whose remission was induced with patients whose remission was maintained. The dissents from risktaker and conservative were explicitly conditioned on a rank-1 placement and are satisfied by this one, which is where both of them put it, and conservative declined to veto outright, calling the clean safety read the opposite of their worry. Of every HA-directed programme in the dossier this is the only one that requires the prior allograft rather than excluding it, which is why TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 are shut to her and this is not.
open_questions: HLA-A*02:01 allele status, unretrieved (the gate)
HA-1 genotype of the patient and the sibling, and whether the mismatch runs recipient-positive / donor-negative
Whether HLA loss or class I downregulation on the relapsed blasts has already made them blind to an A*02:01-restricted product
Whether Fred Hutch runs the rs1801284 typing on both parties during screening, and whether the sibling consents to a fresh collection
The interaction with HCT2 immunosuppression and engraftment, unmeasured in the published series
likelihood_of_effect: Assuming A*02:01 and the HA-1 mismatch confirm: uncertain but curative-intent - 4/9 CR on a feasibility-and-DLT primary endpoint, and no data at 85% blasts.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (grade 3-5 infection after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion, one grade 4 infusion reaction in 9; no CRS, no ICANS, no dose-limiting toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: Tumour burden blunts TCR-T; HLA loss or class I downregulation on relapsed blasts would leave the product blind to HA-1.

overall: The lever the referral was submitted to find, and the only HA-directed protocol requiring her prior graft rather than excluding it - live only if the typing confirms.

intervention_label: Sibling donor lymphocyte infusion after cytoreduction (EBMT therapeutic starting dose 1x10^7 CD3/kg; interferon-gamma-1b + DLI on NCT06529731 as the trial route)
expected_benefit: Schmid 2007 is the only row in this dossier's post-transplant relapse literature with a concurrent untreated comparator: 171 given DLI versus 228 not, 2-year OS 21% +/- 3% against 9% +/- 2%, p=0.04, n=399. Within the DLI group the split is 56% +/- 10% given in remission or with a favourable karyotype against 15% +/- 3% given in aplasia or with active disease.
key_risks: Acute and chronic GVHD, which is the toxicity and the mechanism at the same time; grade III-IV GVHD would close the door on HCT2 and on any post-transplant cellular consolidation
Not one registry row grades adverse events, so the harm cannot be quantified for her from this evidence at all
Marrow aplasia after infusion into a heavily pretreated graft
Cell dose and escalation schedule are centre-specific, so whoever gives it owns the toxicity
preference_alignment: matches curative intent without committing her to a second conditioning regimen: YES; matches prefers_trials: NO at present burden, because the one trial route caps blasts at 30% and allows a single prior post-transplant line she has already spent; no toxicity veto applies.
guideline_status: The EBMT best-practice recommendations on DLI after allogeneic HCT (Practice Harmonisation and Guidelines Committee with the Cellular Therapy and Immunobiology Working Party, Lancet Haematology 2024) are the closest thing to a graded guideline here and set therapeutic sibling DLI at a starting dose of 1x10^7 CD3/kg. NCCN AML v3.2026 carries no DLI recommendation at all, and that silence should not be read as endorsement.
rationale_summary: Three personas ranked sibling DLI and none dissented, which scores higher than the HA-1 product above it, and it is ranked below anyway. Every one of those three endorsements arrives attached to the same finding: the EBMT recommendation is written for MRD-level or post-cytoreduction disease, NCCN carries no DLI recommendation at all, and Schmid's registry puts DLI given in aplasia or with active disease at 15% +/- 3% two-year survival against 56% +/- 10% when given in remission or with a favourable karyotype. Confounding by indication is unadjusted and the design cannot fix it, since the patients who received DLI are the ones their centres judged well enough to receive it. Her late relapse beyond five months puts her on the favourable side of that variable (p<0.0001); roughly 85% blasts and an adverse karyotype put her squarely in the 15% band today. The trial route is shut at present burden, because NCT06529731 caps blasts at 30% by morphology or flow and allows one prior post-transplant salvage line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already spent. Read as a post-cytoreduction lever it stays live, and it is what keeps curative intent on the table if the fitness workup rules out a second conditioning regimen - the 46-patient head-to-head that found no multivariate difference between DLI and HCT2 after debulking is thin, and should not be read as equivalence.
open_questions: Whether cytoreduction gets blasts under 30% and reopens NCT06529731, or under 5% and reopens the whole post-cytoreduction cellular field
Whether HLA class II is still expressed on the blasts - re-infusing the same donor repertoire assumes the antigen presentation that failed once is intact
GVHD risk for her specifically, which no registry row grades
Whether the sibling consents to a second collection, which is also on the HA-1 critical path
likelihood_of_effect: Low as she stands, moderate after cytoreduction: Schmid 2007 puts active-disease DLI at 15% +/- 3% two-year survival against 56% +/- 10% in remission.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (acute and chronic GVHD, marrow aplasia, infection; no registry row grades adverse events, so the harm side is unquantified)

counter_productive_moa.description: Re-infusing the donor repertoire that already stopped holding this disease; grade III-IV GVHD would close the door on HCT2.

overall: The lower-intensity route to graft-versus-leukaemia if fitness rules out a second conditioning regimen, but off-guideline at 85% blasts and shut out of its own trial until the marrow comes down.

scenario_label: If HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed at allele level (no HA-1 mismatch required)
intervention_label: CBX-250, CG1/HLA-A*02:01 x CD3 TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager (CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676)
expected_benefit: No human efficacy readout exists. The case rests on preclinical work: the engager killed HLA-A2-positive primary AML in vitro and in vivo, and the CAR version of the same cathepsin-G leader-sequence target spared normal marrow haematopoiesis.
key_risks: First-in-human dose escalation, so she could sit at a dose level chosen to be safe rather than active
Peptide-HLA engagers have no characterised CRS profile in humans yet, and this would be given into a post-transplant marrow
No published grade-level toxicity of any kind
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials including travel: YES (eleven US sites beat the single Seattle site of the rank-4 option); matches curative intent: PARTIAL (phase 1 escalation); a published compassionate-use route exists, which almost nothing else in this dossier offers.
guideline_status: Investigational, no filing. Enters through NCCN AML v3.2026's clinical-trial-first route for relapsed/refractory disease; no drug-level category exists.
rationale_summary: Advocate ranked this second and risktaker fourth for the same reason: it rides HLA-A*02:01 alone and asks nothing of the sibling, so it is what keeps the A*02:01 handle alive if the HA-1 mismatch runs the wrong way. NCT06994676 names recurrence after HSCT as eligible past 60 days, ECOG 0-1 fits, the extramedullary exclusion applies only to isolated lesions and her marrow involvement takes her out of it, and Crossbow publishes a compassionate-use address for a patient who cannot get a slot. The evidence is the problem and both personas said so in their own rows: no patient has been treated. Status is set to considered_with_caveats rather than the recommended a mechanical read of the endorsement counts would give it, because a first-in-human escalation with no efficacy readout should not carry the same label as an option with published activity. Two gates sit beyond the allele: enrolment wants white cells under 25,000 against peripheral blasts that ran 58 to 82%, so this is post-cytoreduction, and CG1 appears nowhere on her nominated feature list, meaning the pick rides an HLA restriction rather than a validated target in her disease. Ask the sponsor whether CG1 expression is measured on study or whether A*02:01 alone qualifies, so the workup list is complete before anyone books a flight.
open_questions: HLA-A*02:01 allele status (the same gate as rank 4)
Whether CG1 is expressed on her blasts, and whether the protocol measures it or accepts the allele alone
Whether cytoreduction brings white cells under the 25,000 enrolment ceiling
Whether the compassionate-use route is open to a patient who cannot get a slot
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: first-in-human escalation with no efficacy readout. The argument is eligibility fit, eleven US sites and a compassionate-use route, not evidence.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no human safety data; T-cell-engager class cytokine release and infusion reactions expected at high blast burden)

counter_productive_moa.description: Rides HLA-A*02:01 alone, so HLA loss silences it; CG1 expression on these blasts has never been measured.

overall: The A*02:01 option that needs nothing from the sibling and has a compassionate-use route, ranked on eligibility fit and reachability because there is no human efficacy data at all.

intervention_label: BMS-986497 (ORM-6151), CD33-directed antibody-conjugated GSPT1 degrader, monotherapy arm (NCT06419634)
expected_benefit: No published clinical data of any kind. What it offers is eligibility: MDS-related secondary AML named in the inclusion criteria, CD33 required only to be detectable rather than above a threshold, ECOG <=2, and no blast cap or prior-allograft bar in the posted criteria.
key_risks: First-in-human, so no efficacy or toxicity figure exists to quote
GSPT1 degradation is broadly cytotoxic and on-target CD33 killing hits normal myeloid progenitors
Trial-arm assignment may not be hers to choose; the azacitidine-venetoclax triplet would re-expose her to a drug she progressed through
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials including travel: YES; independent of the HLA answer, which matters because ranks 4 and 6 both stand or fall on one allele: YES; no toxicity veto applies.
guideline_status: Investigational, IND-stage, no filing. NCCN AML v3.2026 clinical-trial-first route; no drug-level category.
rationale_summary: Advocate ranked this fifth as the trial fallback that does not depend on the HLA answer at all, which matters because ranks 4 and 6 both stand or fall on one allele. The posted criteria are unusually open for this dossier: MDS-related secondary AML is named in the inclusion criteria, CD33 only has to be detectable rather than above a threshold, ECOG 2 is permitted, and no blast cap or prior-allograft bar appears - rare across the 47 trials screened, and worth confirming with the site rather than assuming. Push for the monotherapy arm rather than the azacitidine-venetoclax triplet, since she progressed through venetoclax and re-exposing her would spend a trial slot on a drug that has already failed. No persona dissented and none vetoed, but there is no published clinical data of any kind, so this ranks on eligibility fit and reachability rather than on evidence, and she should hear it framed that way. Enrolling consumes weeks an 85% marrow may not have, so it competes with the rank-2 cytoreduction on time rather than complementing it.
open_questions: Whether the absent exclusions in the posted criteria survive contact with the site
Whether she can be assigned to the monotherapy arm rather than the venetoclax-containing triplet
Quantitative CD33 density, which the protocol does not require but which predicts CD33-ADC activity
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: first-in-human with no published clinical data. Listed because it is open, reachable and independent of the pending HLA answer.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no published clinical safety; CD33-ADC and GSPT1-degrader class myelosuppression and hepatic risk expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target CD33 killing of normal myeloid progenitors could deepen aplasia and delay the graft; no mechanism objection was raised.

overall: The CD33 trial fallback that does not depend on the pending allele, with unusually open posted criteria and no clinical data behind it whatsoever.

intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate) at the 0.045 mg/kg RP2D, off-label after the May 2026 BPDCN approval
expected_benefit: Own-disease data, which no other CD123 agent here can show: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% (6-36) in 29 patients at the recommended phase 2 dose in relapsed/refractory CD123-positive AML. Response was secondary to an MTD/RP2D primary endpoint.
key_risks: Hepatic veno-occlusive disease: two dose-limiting events in 68 patients, both at 0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg (four to ten times the 0.045 mg/kg RP2D) and both reversible; the US label carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including hepatic VOD
At the RP2D, grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion-related reactions 7%, anaemia 7%
No baseline bilirubin, transaminases or albumin on file, and a second conditioning regimen is planned
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-stated handle and the efficacy-leaning debulking rationale: YES; matches prefers_trials: NO (the AML cohorts are closed to accrual, so this would be off-label use); no toxicity veto applies, since the list is empty.
guideline_status: FDA-approved 27 May 2026 as DECNUPAZ for BPDCN only, with a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including hepatic veno-occlusive disease. No AML indication, no NCCN AML or ELN listing - off-label and investigational for this patient.
rationale_summary: Critic ranked pivekimab fourth on the strength of its own-disease data, ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% in 29 patients at the RP2D, which is more than any other CD123 agent here can show in her indication. Conservative dissented on hepatic grounds, arguing that two dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68 patients is the wrong exposure in the weeks before a conditioning regimen. Risktaker corrected the read and the correction holds: both events occurred at 0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg, four to ten times the 0.045 mg/kg RP2D, and both were reversible, so this is a dose-level finding rather than a property of the drug, and striking CD123 out of the pre-conditioning window on it is an over-read. The personas ran concurrently, so conservative never saw that correction; adjudicating it, the dissent is sustained in narrowed form rather than as a bar, and no veto was issued in this run. What survives is specific and checkable: pivekimab's label carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including hepatic VOD, and there is no pre-transplant hepatic series for it comparable to the 57 fractionated-gemtuzumab patients of whom seven were transplanted afterwards, so baseline bilirubin and transaminases with weekly monitoring are the condition rather than exclusion. An interval running from 8% to 40% on n=29 is too soft to displace the rank-2 cytoreduction, so hold it as the fallback if quantitative CD33 density comes back low.
open_questions: Baseline bilirubin, transaminases and albumin - the condition on which the narrowed hepatic dissent turns
Quantitative CD123 antigen density, unmeasured; the 75% frontline BPDCN figure is a different disease and must not be carried across
Whether any enrolling AML cohort or expanded-access route reopens, since the AML studies are closed to accrual
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate as debulking: the only CD123 agent with own-disease data (ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40; cCR 17%), but the interval carries little information on n=29.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (hepatic veno-occlusive disease at four to ten times the RP2D, both events reversible; at the RP2D grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion reactions 7%, anaemia 7%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Hepatic veno-occlusive disease before conditioning could cost the transplant the debulking is meant to enable.

overall: The only CD123 agent with data in her own disease and line, held under a narrowed hepatic condition rather than a bar: liver labs and weekly monitoring first.

intervention_label: Tagraxofusp (SL-401, CD123-directed IL-3 / diphtheria-toxin fusion), off-label in AML or via the R/R AML cohort of NCT03113643
expected_benefit: First-line CR / clinical CR 72% (21/29) at 12 mcg/kg in BPDCN, which is cross-tumour read-across rather than indication data. The nearest AML number is 69% overall response with azacitidine with or without venetoclax in untreated AML (n=26), a different line from hers.
key_risks: Capillary leak syndrome in 19% (boxed warning), with a fatal case reported in each dose subgroup
Transaminase elevation (ALT 64%, AST 60% any grade) and hypoalbuminaemia 55%
No baseline albumin, cardiac or hepatic workup on file, and the NCT03113643 cohort requires albumin above 3.2 g/dL
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-stated handle: YES; matches prefers_trials via the R/R AML cohort of NCT03113643: PARTIAL (prior venetoclax excludes unless the last dose was more than two months ago); off-label cross-tumour use tempers the alignment.
guideline_status: FDA- and EMA-approved in BPDCN only. No NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing, so AML use is off-label cross-tumour read-across.
rationale_summary: No persona ranked tagraxofusp in round 1, and risktaker passed it over explicitly, calling it weaker cytoreduction than CLAG-GO for someone who needs the marrow emptied fast. It is surfaced and ranked here anyway because CD123 is a user-stated handle, the drug has an FDA label with a worked-out capillary-leak management algorithm and years of post-marketing safety, and NCT03113643 has an open R/R AML cohort where CD123 expression is the only biomarker gate. The number people quote is BPDCN, not AML: 72% CR or clinical CR at 12 mcg/kg in first-line BPDCN, cross-tumour read-across that says nothing about an 85%-blast AML marrow. The AML-specific data are thinner and in a different line, 69% overall response with azacitidine with or without venetoclax in untreated AML on 26 patients. Conservative named the practical gate, that the tagraxofusp cohort on NCT03113643 requires albumin above 3.2 g/dL, and prior venetoclax excludes unless the last dose was more than two months ago, which this patient's FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax may or may not satisfy. Off-label in AML with no NCCN or ELN listing, so this is investigational for her rather than standard care, and presenting the BPDCN figure as an expectation would misstate its footing.
open_questions: Quantitative CD123 antigen density, which spans roughly 200 to 10,000 molecules per cell across AML and is what agent selection turns on
Baseline albumin (the NCT03113643 gate is >3.2 g/dL) plus cardiac and hepatic reserve before a capillary-leak-prone therapy
Whether the venetoclax washout on NCT03113643 is satisfied
Whether cross-tumour BPDCN efficacy transfers to high-burden AML at all
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-uncertain in AML: the headline 72% CR is first-line BPDCN cross-tumour, and the nearest AML data (69% ORR, n=26) are untreated disease.
toxicity_burden: High (capillary leak syndrome 19% with a fatal case in each dose subgroup, transaminitis ALT 64% / AST 60%, hypoalbuminaemia 55%)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanistic antagonism; on-target killing of normal CD34+CD123+ progenitors adds myelosuppression ahead of a graft.

overall: The only labelled CD123 agent with a real capillary-leak management algorithm, but its headline number is BPDCN cross-tumour and it needs an albumin and cardiac baseline first.

intervention_label: 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) targeted conditioning ahead of haploidentical allogeneic HCT (NCT03670966)
expected_benefit: No published human efficacy for 211At-BC8-B10. The borrowed principle is SIERRA: durable CR 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) with 131I-apamistamab conditioning against 0% (0-4.7) on conventional care, p<0.0001, in patients who had active disease at randomisation. The primary preclinical support is a syngeneic mouse transplant with a murine anti-CD45 (median survival 123, 101, 61 and 37 days at 24, 20, 12 and 0 microCi).
key_risks: Alpha-emitter dosimetry plus a second graft in a heavily pretreated marrow: unquantified cytopenia and non-relapse mortality risk
In SIERRA, overall survival did not separate at all (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41, p=0.96) even where the durable-CR difference was stark
Circulating blasts must be under 10,000/mm3, which at 82% peripheral blasts means hydroxyurea has to work first
Myeloablative conditioning in 2020 would exclude her, and the profile does not record what she was given
preference_alignment: matches curative intent and prefers_trials including travel: YES; matches the no-modality-ruled-out statement: YES; but the protocol wants a haploidentical relative rather than the HLA-identical sibling, which is a donor question nobody has asked.
guideline_status: Investigational, no filing. The FDA determined the SIERRA analyses did not support a BLA filing and required an additional randomised study showing an overall-survival benefit (announced August 2024). No guideline carries targeted radioimmunotherapy conditioning.
rationale_summary: Risktaker ranked this fifth on a principle SIERRA actually proved: durable CR 17.1% versus 0% with antigen-targeted conditioning in patients who had active disease at randomisation, which is the problem nobody can cytoreduce their way out of. Both dissents landed on transportability rather than the principle. Conservative withdrew the veto they had pre-registered, cleanly - it was conditioned on a rank-1 pick taking her to conditioning at 85% blasts on the strength of Iomab-B, and at rank 5, with human efficacy for 211At-BC8-B10 stated as nil, the condition is not met - and kept a dissent, because SIERRA excluded prior allo-HCT and NCT07157514 excludes it again while capping blasts at 20%, so the randomised 17.1% cannot be quoted for her at any rank. Critic dissented on the same axis and added that overall survival did not move in SIERRA at all (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41, p=0.96), that the FDA declined the filing and asked for an OS study, and that 211At-BC8-B10 then inherits the principle with nothing behind it but a syngeneic mouse transplant using a murine anti-CD45. What keeps it on the list rather than in a footnote is that NCT03670966 is the one targeted-conditioning protocol admitting a prior reduced-intensity allograft, provided there is no ongoing GVHD and six weeks off immunosuppression. Two hard gates: the protocol wants a haploidentical relative rather than the sibling who gave the 2020 graft, and circulating blasts must be under 10,000/mm3. Whether such a relative exists is worth a phone call now rather than a discovery in three months.
open_questions: Whether a haploidentical relative exists, since the sibling who gave the 2020 graft does not satisfy the protocol
What conditioning she received in 2020 - myeloablative conditioning would exclude her
Whether hydroxyurea brings circulating blasts under 10,000/mm3
Whether any human efficacy readout for 211At-BC8-B10 has been posted since the dossier was assembled
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown for this construct: no human efficacy published. The borrowed SIERRA signal (dCR 17.1% vs 0%) came from a population that excluded prior allo-HCT.
toxicity_burden: High (alpha-emitter conditioning plus a second graft: prolonged aplasia, infection and non-relapse mortality; no human adverse-event table published for this construct)

counter_productive_moa.description: Alpha-emitter marrow injury before a second graft in a heavily pretreated marrow; needs a haploidentical relative, not the existing sibling.

overall: The one targeted-conditioning protocol that admits her prior graft, carrying a principle SIERRA proved in a population that excluded her and no human efficacy of its own.

intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, TP53 Y220C-selective p53 reactivator) + azacitidine (NCT06616636) - considered and declined
expected_benefit: None quotable. No peer-reviewed clinical effect size exists for rezatapopt in myeloid disease; the interim response rates in circulation are sponsor communications, and the parent PYNNACLE study requires RECIST-measurable disease that a marrow-based leukaemia cannot provide.
key_risks: No published clinical toxicity in myeloid disease; azacitidine-backbone cytopenias apply
An azacitidine backbone is slow against 85% blasts in refractory disease, which sits badly against a stated curative intent
A trial slot spent on a mechanism that needed venetoclax to kill in the only mechanistic study available
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES in form; matches curative intent: NO in substance, because the azacitidine backbone is slow against 85% blasts and the partner drug the mechanism needs is the one she progressed through.
guideline_status: Investigational, no approval. For poor-risk AML with TP53 mutation or del(17p), NCCN AML v3.2026 lists clinical trial and nothing else, which is the hook concensusite used in round 1 and which still stands after they withdrew this particular trial for this patient absent a variant call.
rationale_summary: Concensusite ranked rezatapopt fifth in round 1 as the trial-shaped answer NCCN points at for TP53-aberrant poor-risk AML, framed from the outset as contingent on a Y220C call that does not exist in either direction, then withdrew the pick outright in round 2, calling the assay-decides-eligibility problem decisive. Risktaker and conservative dissented on converging grounds, and this is recorded as considered-and-declined rather than dropped. Carter 2025 restored wild-type conformation in Y220C AML and got limited or absent apoptosis unless venetoclax or an MDM2/XPO1 partner was added, and venetoclax is the drug she just progressed through, so even a positive Y220C call leaves the pick without a partner. NCT06616636 screens on a CLIA Y220C call at VAF above 2%, which sits at the detection limit of the same class of panel that returned her 2026 TP53-negative result, so the assay could decide eligibility before the biology does. No peer-reviewed clinical effect size exists anywhere for the agent in myeloid disease. Declining it does not collapse the TP53 branch in either direction: the rank-1 workup still retrieves the 2019 variant identity and VAF, adds p53 IHC, 17p FISH and a copy-number-capable panel, and a confirmed Y220C would reopen this row with an MDM2 or XPO1 partner rather than azacitidine.
open_questions: Whether the 2019 TP53 lesion was Y220C (the 2019 variant table has never been retrieved)
Whether a copy-number-capable panel, p53 IHC or 17p FISH explains the 2026 negative result
Whether an MDM2 or XPO1 partner combination becomes available, since the mechanism needs one and venetoclax is spent
Eprenetapopt is not the fallback: that programme stopped after the randomised phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint
likelihood_of_effect: Not assessable: no peer-reviewed clinical effect size in myeloid disease, and the only mechanistic study needed venetoclax for killing - the drug she just failed.
toxicity_burden: Low (none extractable - no peer-reviewed clinical toxicity in myeloid disease; azacitidine-backbone cytopenias apply)

counter_productive_moa.description: Reactivated Y220C p53 restored conformation with limited or no apoptosis unless venetoclax was added, the agent she just progressed through.

overall: Declined, not dropped: double-gated on a Y220C call at the detection limit of the panel that called her negative, and needing venetoclax to kill.

intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2 TCR-T commercial and next-generation products (TSC-100 and TSC-101 on ALLOHA/NCT05473910, BSB-1001 on NCT06704152, MDG1021 on the withdrawn NCT04464889)
expected_benefit: Not applicable - she cannot enrol. The class rationale is the same as rank 4: a minor-histocompatibility antigen restricted to blood-lineage cells, delivering graft-versus-leukaemia without broad GVHD.
key_risks: Prior allogeneic HCT is an exclusion on TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001
BSB-1001 additionally caps myeloblasts at 25%
MDG1021 withdrawn without enrolling
preference_alignment: matches the stated HLA-restricted priority in principle: YES; enrollable: NO.
guideline_status: Investigational, no FDA or EMA filing for any agent in the class.
rationale_summary: These are the HA-directed products that get the attention, and every one of them shuts her out on the same criterion. TSC-100/101 exclude prior allogeneic HCT and are built around haploidentical, mismatched-unrelated or matched-unrelated donors rather than an HLA-identical sibling. BSB-1001 excludes prior allogeneic transplant outright and separately caps myeloblasts at 25% against a marrow of roughly 85%. MDG1021 was the one HA-1 protocol written specifically for sibling-donor recipients at least 100 days post-transplant, and it was withdrawn without enrolling a patient. Critic added a methodological correction the board should keep: the HA-2 arm rests on a 2003 in vitro paper describing a different TCR from the one in the clinical product, so HA-1 and HA-2 are not equivalently evidenced. The enrollable version of this approach is the rank-4 Bleakley platform, which requires the prior graft rather than excluding it.
open_questions: Whether any sponsor opens a post-transplant cohort
Whether the HA-2 genotype matters at all once the HA-1 direction is known
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: prior allo-HCT is an exclusion on every commercial HA-directed protocol; the HA-2 arm additionally rests on a different TCR.
toxicity_burden: Low (no clinical data; class safety carried by the rank-4 Bleakley platform)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss escape possible; lineage-restricted killing limits collateral. No mechanism objection raised.

overall: The HA-directed products she cannot have: all three exclude prior allogeneic HCT, which is exactly what the rank-4 protocol requires.

intervention_label: WT1-directed HLA-A*02:01-restricted TCR-T (WT1-TCRC4 / TTCR-C4 on the terminated NCT01640301; successor FH-WT1-E50 + azacitidine on NCT07645469)
expected_benefit: Not enrollable now. If cytoreduction reaches morphologic remission with detectable MRD, NCT07645469 becomes a conversation.
key_risks: Grade 3 acute GVHD reported in the prophylaxis cohort
No dose-limiting toxicity or product-related serious AEs in the active-disease cohort (n=15)
preference_alignment: matches the stated WT1 handle: YES; enrollable at present disease state: NO.
guideline_status: Investigational; the predecessor trial is terminated and no guideline lists WT1 TCR-T.
rationale_summary: Two published cohorts, and the gap between them is the whole point. Chapuis 2019 reported 100% relapse-free survival at a median 44 months in 12 patients, but that was prophylaxis into patients already in remission after transplant. Mazziotta 2025 gave the same TCR to post-HCT disease (n=15, median OS 242 days, 2-year OS 33%, 3-year 20%) and states it did not clearly improve outcomes, and even that cohort had only 2 of 15 with overt disease. Citing the first figure for this patient would be citing the wrong population, which is the correction critic filed. The open successor, FH-WT1-E50, requires morphologic remission with under 5% marrow blasts and detectable MRD, so it is a consolidation-phase option after a deep response rather than a route from here. This is also the load-bearing evidence behind risktaker's tumour-burden argument at rank 4.
open_questions: Whether cytoreduction reaches under 5% blasts with detectable MRD
Whether WT1 is overexpressed on her blasts (ELN-standardised qPCR is in the rank-1 workup)
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable at 85% blasts: the open successor requires morphologic remission with MRD, and the active-disease cohort showed median OS 242 days.
toxicity_burden: Low (no dose-limiting toxicity and no product-related serious adverse events across n=15; grade 3 acute GVHD in the prophylaxis cohort)

counter_productive_moa.description: The class did little against active disease; WT1 is also broadly expressed on normal progenitors, risking on-target myelosuppression.

overall: The WT1 arm of the A*02:01 axis, and the cohort that supplies the tumour-burden argument used against ranking cellular therapy ahead of cytoreduction.

intervention_label: WT1-siTCR gene-transduced lymphocytes (TBI-1301), HLA-A*24:02-restricted
expected_benefit: Transient marrow blast reduction in 2 of 8 refractory patients, with no normal-tissue toxicity reported.
key_risks: No normal-tissue adverse events reported across n=8
No accessible route for a US patient
preference_alignment: matches the stated WT1 handle and the profile's explicit instruction to resolve A*24:02 in parallel: YES; enrollable: NO.
guideline_status: Investigational; Japanese academic and industry development, no US or EU filing for the WT1 product.
rationale_summary: This is the one WT1 handle that does not need HLA-A*02:01, and it is the reason profile.json insists both alleles be resolved before HLA-restricted immunotherapy is written off. Tawara 2017 infused 8 patients with refractory AML and high-risk MDS and reported transient marrow blast reductions in 2 with no normal-tissue adverse events. Advocate declined to rank it and said why: the accessibility read is Japan-only with no enrolling study a US patient can enter, and telling her a door is open when the sponsor is not opening it would be worse than telling her it is shut. Keep it on the record anyway, because if the retrieved typing comes back A*02:01-negative and A*24:02-positive, this is the only HLA-restricted thread left worth pulling and the answer would be a sponsor enquiry rather than an enrolment.
open_questions: HLA-A*24:02 allele status, pulled in parallel in the rank-1 workup
Whether the sponsor would consider a named-patient route
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: Japan-only development with no US or EU route. Route-preservation only - transient blast reductions in 2 of 8.
toxicity_burden: Low (no normal-tissue adverse events reported across n=8)

counter_productive_moa.description: The siTCR design silences the endogenous TCR and spared normal tissue in the published series.

overall: The A*24:02 fallback that keeps an immunotherapy thread alive if A*02:01 types negative, with no route a US patient can currently enter.

intervention_label: MDG1011 (PRAME-directed, HLA-A*02:01-restricted autologous TCR-T) and BPX-701 (PRAME TCR-T with an iCasp9 switch)
expected_benefit: Not obtainable. MDG1011 reported measurable clinical response in 2 of 9 (22.2%) before the programme stopped.
key_risks: CRS in 2 of 9 in the MDG1011 phase 1; no dose-limiting toxicity
Programme discontinued - no route
preference_alignment: matches the stated PRAME handle: YES; obtainable: NO.
guideline_status: Investigational; development stopped, no filing.
rationale_summary: Both PRAME programmes are dead. MDG1011 completed phase 1 with a measurable clinical response in 2 of 9 patients and stopped rather than advancing, and its own investigators attributed the outcome to tumour burden - which is the second half of the argument risktaker used at rank 4. BPX-701 was terminated by company decision after four patients, though its eligibility is worth reading, since AML with a prior transplant was allowed past day 100 without active GVHD, one of the few PRAME protocols that did not treat a prior graft as disqualifying. Note also that MDG1011 excluded patients planned for allogeneic HSCT, which would have sat awkwardly against a curative HCT2 intent even had it stayed open. PRAME expression on her blasts has never been measured; the rank-1 workup adds it as a reflex read after HLA typing.
open_questions: Whether PRAME is expressed on her blasts at all (reflex RNA read in the rank-1 workup)
Whether any successor PRAME product opens a post-transplant cohort
likelihood_of_effect: Not obtainable: both PRAME TCR-T programmes discontinued. MDG1011 reached 22.2% measurable response in 9 patients before stopping.
toxicity_burden: Low (no dose-limiting toxicity across n=9; cytokine release in 2 of 9)

counter_productive_moa.description: The sponsor's own reading was that tumour burden limited activity, the same failure mode that shapes the rank-4 sequencing.

overall: The PRAME half of the stated HLA-restricted handle, closed on both sides - and the source of the tumour-burden argument that set the sequencing.

intervention_label: Donor-derived and off-the-shelf multi-leukaemia-antigen-specific T cells (TAA-T on NCT02203903, ADSPAM on NCT02494167, MT-401-OTS on NCT06552416)
expected_benefit: Lulla 2021: objective response in 2 of 8 in the active-disease cohort; median leukaemia-free and overall survival not reached at 1.9 years across n=25.
key_risks: No grade >2 acute GVHD and no extensive chronic GVHD across 25 recipients
Every open protocol excludes her on disease state, age or second-transplant plans
preference_alignment: matches the stated WT1/PRAME handles and prefers_trials: YES; enrollable: NO on all three open protocols.
guideline_status: Investigational, no filing. NCCN AML v3.2026 clinical-trial-first route; no drug-level category.
rationale_summary: The appeal is real: these products prime T cells against PRAME, WT1, Survivin and NY-ESO-1 at once, so they hit two of her stated handles without depending on a single HLA restriction, and Lulla 2021 reported an objective response in 2 of 8 patients with active disease and no grade >2 acute GVHD across 25 recipients. Every open route is shut on a criterion she cannot change. NCT02203903 requires patients who have NOT had a haematologic relapse after transplant and separately excludes anyone who has received or will receive a second allogeneic HSCT, which is the plan. MT-401-OTS caps marrow blasts at 10% and peripheral blasts at 5% and requires age 65 or older, and she is in the 50-59 band. ADSPAM is the one written for post-transplant relapse and counting extramedullary sites as qualifying disease, which would suit the thigh lesion, and it is active but not recruiting. Worth re-checking ADSPAM's status if cytoreduction succeeds.
open_questions: Whether ADSPAM (NCT02494167) reopens to accrual
Whether cytoreduction brings blasts under the MT-401-OTS ceiling, which would still leave the age criterion
WT1 and PRAME expression on the blasts
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: the open protocols exclude post-transplant relapse, a planned second HCT, or cap blasts at 10%. Modest activity (2/8) in active disease.
toxicity_burden: Low (no grade >2 acute GVHD and no extensive chronic GVHD across n=25)

counter_productive_moa.description: Multi-antigen targeting limits single-antigen escape; no mechanism that blunts the goal.

overall: The HLA-independent hedge that hits WT1 and PRAME at once, locked behind disease-state, age and second-transplant exclusions on every open protocol.

intervention_label: GLIDE (guided lymphocyte immunopeptide-derived expansion; donor anti-minor-histocompatibility-antigen T cells, NCT03091933)
expected_benefit: None published. The design accepts nineteen class I alleles rather than requiring A*02:01.
key_risks: No published clinical data
Registry status unknown; academic programme with no filing
preference_alignment: matches the stated HLA-restricted priority and would survive an A*02:01-negative result: YES; obtainable: NO.
guideline_status: Investigational; academic programme with no filing.
rationale_summary: On paper the eligibility reads like it was written for her: prior HLA-matched transplant, at least six months out, detectable relapse, original donor available, ECOG 2 or better, no prior DLI. It also sidesteps the A*02:01 bottleneck by accepting any of nineteen class I alleles including A*24:02. The registry status is unknown and the programme is academic with no filing, so there is nothing to enrol into today. It is recorded because the design is the closest thing in this dossier to an HLA-agnostic minor-antigen approach, and because a status change would matter more here than for most rows.
open_questions: Whether the trial is still open in any form
Whether her class I type falls in the nineteen-allele set once typing returns
likelihood_of_effect: Not obtainable: registry status unknown, academic programme with no filing. Design is the only HLA-agnostic minor-antigen route in the dossier.
toxicity_burden: Low (no published clinical toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: Minor-antigen T cells carry GVHD risk in principle; no data either way.

overall: The one minor-antigen approach that does not bottleneck on A*02:01, with no current route and an unknown registry status.

intervention_label: CD123-directed CAR-T and switchable CD123 CAR platforms (Allo-RevCAR01-T + R-TM123, NCT05949125)
expected_benefit: No published clinical efficacy. The design argument is a soluble target module that can be withdrawn to switch the CAR off.
key_risks: No published clinical safety data
CAR-T class cytokine release and lymphodepletion cytopenias
On-target killing of normal CD123+ progenitors
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-stated handle and prefers_trials including travel: YES; evidence: none published.
guideline_status: Investigational; no approved CD123 CAR product.
rationale_summary: An off-the-shelf CD123 CAR with a soluble targeting module that can be switched off, which is a meaningful safety design for a patient carrying a heavy blast burden. ECOG 0-1 matches, and the extramedullary exclusion applies only to AML with solely extramedullary manifestations, so the thigh sarcoma alongside marrow disease does not disqualify her. What is missing is any published clinical efficacy for the construct, so it cannot carry a live rank. No persona ranked it. open_questions: Quantitative CD123 antigen density
Whether the site accepts a patient six years out from allo-HCT
Whether any efficacy readout has posted
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: no published clinical efficacy for the construct. Recruiting, with a switchable design that addresses on-target myelosuppression.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no published grade profile; CAR-T class cytokine release syndrome and lymphodepletion cytopenias expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target killing of normal CD123+ progenitors adds myelosuppression; the switchable module is designed to limit it.

overall: A switchable off-the-shelf CD123 CAR that is recruiting and eligible on disease state, with no published clinical efficacy to rank on.

intervention_label: VIP943 (CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate, NCT06034275)
expected_benefit: No published clinical efficacy.
key_risks: No published clinical data
Sponsor initiated wind-down activities in 2025; registry entry stale
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-stated handle and prefers_trials: YES; obtainable: doubtful.

Vitruvias initiated wind-down activities in 2025 and the listed completion date has passed without the registry entry being updated, so the trial's operational status cannot be relied on. open_questions: Whether the site is still enrolling despite the sponsor wind-down
likelihood_of_effect: Not reliably obtainable: sponsor wind-down in 2025 with a stale registry entry, despite eligibility criteria that fit her unusually well.
toxicity_burden: Low (no published clinical toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: CD123-ADC on-target myelosuppression; no mechanism objection raised.

overall: A CD123 ADC whose posted criteria fit her better than most, on a programme the sponsor began winding down in 2025.

intervention_label: Flotetuzumab (MGD006, CD123 x CD3 DART)
expected_benefit: CR/CRh 26.7% in 30 chemorefractory patients (primary induction failure or early relapse); 47% CR in a 15-patient post-hoc TP53-abnormal subgroup with no confidence interval.
key_risks: Infusion-related reactions or cytokine release in 96% at the RP2D, 8% grade 3+, managed with step-up dosing
Programme discontinued - no route
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-stated handle: YES; obtainable: NO.
guideline_status: Investigational; development discontinued, no filing.
rationale_summary: The most interesting number in this dossier belongs to a drug that no longer exists, and risktaker was right to say someone should record that. Flotetuzumab produced CR/CRh in 26.7% of 30 patients with primary induction failure or early relapse, which is exactly the population she sits in, and MacroGenics terminated the programme in 2022 for business reasons. The TP53 figure needs handling: 47% CR in TP53-abnormal relapsed/refractory AML is a post-hoc correlative read on 15 patients with no confidence interval reported, and critic filed that correction explicitly, so it should not be cited as a TP53-specific effect size for anything. The live version of this mechanism is the rank-6 CG1/A*02:01 engager, which is a different target on the same redirection principle.
open_questions: Whether any successor CD123xCD3 construct opens in refractory post-transplant AML
likelihood_of_effect: Not obtainable (discontinued): CR/CRh 26.7% in exactly her chemorefractory population; the 47% TP53 figure is post-hoc on 15 patients.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (infusion-related reactions or cytokine release in 96%, grade 3+ in 8%, managed with step-up dosing and tocilizumab)

counter_productive_moa.description: CD123xCD3 redirection needs fit T cells; post-transplant and post-FLAG-IDA exhaustion may blunt it. TP53 rationale is post-hoc.

overall: A discontinued drug carrying the most relevant salvage number in the file, and the reason to chase an open CD123 or peptide-HLA engager instead.

intervention_label: Vibecotamab (XmAb14045, CD123 x CD3 bispecific)
expected_benefit: ORR 9.0% across 120 patients in relapsed/refractory AML.
key_risks: Cytokine release in 85%, grade 3+ in 26.7% including one grade 5
Programme terminated for under-accrual
preference_alignment: matches CD123 as a user-stated handle: YES; obtainable: NO.

Its own phase 1 read ORR 9.0% across 120 patients with relapsed/refractory AML, with cytokine release in 85% and grade 3+ in 26.7%, which is a worse trade than the flotetuzumab row above it. toxicity_burden: High (cytokine release syndrome 85% any grade, 26.7% grade 3+ including one grade 5)

overall: The second CD123 bispecific to stop, with the weakest activity and the heaviest cytokine-release burden of the class.

intervention_label: CD33-directed CAR-T (CART-33 and successors, NCT05672147)
expected_benefit: One published patient: marked marrow blast reduction at two weeks, progression by nine weeks.
key_risks: Chills, fever and cytokine elevation in the single published patient
On-target CD33 killing of normal myeloid progenitors ahead of a planned graft
preference_alignment: matches CD33 as a user-stated handle and prefers_trials including travel: YES; evidence: n=1.

intervention_label: 131I-apamistamab (Iomab-B) anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning before allogeneic HCT
expected_benefit: Durable CR 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care, p<0.0001, n=153; overall survival flat at HR 0.99 (0.70-1.41).
key_risks: Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events 59.7% versus 59.2% on conventional care
Prior allogeneic HCT excluded from SIERRA and from the successor protocol
Successor caps marrow blasts at 20%
preference_alignment: matches curative intent and the HCT2 platform handle: YES; obtainable: NO on both the closed and successor protocols.
guideline_status: Not approved. The FDA determined the SIERRA analyses did not adequately support a BLA filing and required an additional randomised study showing an overall-survival benefit (August 2024).
rationale_summary: SIERRA is the only phase 3 in this file that hit its registered primary endpoint: durable CR 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% (0-4.7) on physician's-choice conventional care, p<0.0001, n=153, with grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events at 59.7% against 59.2% on conventional care. Overall survival did not move at all (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41, p=0.96), the FDA determined the analyses did not support a filing and required a randomised OS study, and prior allogeneic HCT was an exclusion. The successor NCT07157514 excludes prior HSCT again and caps marrow blasts between 5% and 20% against roughly 85% here, so the mismatch is not marginal. High design tier, no route, and no support for use in this patient - which matters mainly for expectation-setting, since Iomab-B gets discussed as though it were available for anyone with active disease.
open_questions: Whether any protocol opens targeted CD45 conditioning to a second transplant
likelihood_of_effect: Not obtainable: the only phase 3 to hit its primary endpoint (dCR 17.1% vs 0%) excluded prior allo-HCT, and the successor excludes it again.
toxicity_burden: High (grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events 59.7%, at parity with conventional care; conditioning cytopenias, infection, mucositis)

counter_productive_moa.description: Radioconjugate marrow injury before engraftment; the trial-level problem is flat overall survival, not mechanism antagonism.

overall: The strongest design tier in the dossier, closed to her on both protocols and with flat overall survival even where the durable-CR difference was stark.

intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC sequential conditioning (fludarabine/cytarabine/amsacrine into reduced-intensity conditioning; US analogues DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC on NCT06928662 and FLAMSAClax on NCT05807932)
expected_benefit: CR in 66 of 75 patients (88%) after sequential conditioning, 59 with progressive or refractory disease, and 42% alive at two years.
key_risks: Non-relapse mortality of a second graft, unchanged by the sequencing
Repeating a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through
Amsacrine is not marketed in the US
preference_alignment: matches curative intent and the HCT2 platform handle: YES; matches prefers_trials via NCT06928662: PARTIAL.
guideline_status: Sequential-conditioning strategy assembled from individually approved agents; no NCCN or ELN category attaches to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse.
rationale_summary: This is the sequential-conditioning form of the rank-3 transplant approach rather than a separate option, which is why it is consolidated rather than scored on its own. The evidence is the reason risktaker wanted the aggressive version: cytoreduction running straight into reduced-intensity conditioning produced CR in 66 of 75 patients, 59 of whom had progressive or refractory disease, with 42% alive at two years. Amsacrine is not marketed in the United States, so the reachable form is NCT06928662 or an institutional sequential regimen. FLAMSAClax (NCT05807932) is shut to her twice over: it demands patients essentially untreated apart from hydroxyurea or up to two cycles of a hypomethylating agent, and excludes marrow blasts above 30%. NCT06928662 asks her to repeat a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through, which is a clinical objection to raise with the investigator rather than an access one.
open_questions: Whether the investigator will substitute the cytoreduction rather than repeat FLAG-Ida
Whether a measured ejection fraction and creatinine clearance permit sequential conditioning at all
likelihood_of_effect: Consolidated into rank 3: the sequential-conditioning form of the ranked transplant approach. CR 88% (66/75) in largely refractory disease, 42% alive at two years.
toxicity_burden: High (second-graft non-relapse mortality, GVHD, prolonged cytopenias, infection)

counter_productive_moa.description: Repeating the FLAG-Ida backbone she progressed through risks buying the conditioning toxicity without the cytoreduction.

overall: The sequential-conditioning route into the ranked second transplant: reachable in the US only as DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC or an institutional regimen, and it repeats a backbone she failed.
